Class EventLoopSafety

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.python.processing.staticcompile.EventLoopSafety
@Internal public final class EventLoopSafety extends Object
Which compiled bodies never enter Python, so that a route whose body is one runs on the event loop as a Java route does. A body never enters Python when nothing in it does by itself, every compiled body of the compilation it calls through Java never does either, and every generated constructor it calls only assigns Java fields; a cycle of calls does not count as safe. The planner records what it knows of the calls of the compilation a body makes through Java (Ir.PythonEntries), and pythonEntry(Ir.CompiledBody, Predicate) finds what runs Python where the body stands:
  • a call or a read through the Python object (Ir.InvokePython, Ir.PythonMember, a sibling dispatched python);
  • a read of an attribute of self that is not fixed at construction, or a property, and an assignment of one;
  • a raise of a Python exception class that creates the exception through its Python class (a lazy one, Ir.NewPythonException.lazy(), creates the Java exception alone);
  • a read of a constant of a generated class;
  • rendering, comparing or hashing a value whose type names a generated class or Object: its toString, equals or hashCode may be the Python object's.
A read of an attribute fixed at construction is allowed: the stub primes its slot when it takes its Python object, off the request (see PythonFixedAttributes#prime), and the runtime keeps a route on the event loop only when its bean is a singleton created at startup (PythonEventLoopBeans). The slot reads the Python object again only after code outside the compilation assigns the attribute, which the compilation never does. An injected attribute of a module is a Java field of the module's generated class, set when the module is injected.
